initial_review.scope: Next named-style-map arithmetic boundary: source review and reproduced AddStyle mismatch, not a completed correction.
confirmed_source_differences: Rust computes the high threshold in every insert and the low threshold in every successful removal; ATL caches both.
ATL updates thresholds in SetOptimalLoad, InitHashTable and successful Rehash. Its constructor calls SetOptimalLoad; compiler folding of default constants still needs direct constructor observations.

The native bins pointer is initially null and becomes null again on RemoveAll. First insertion allocates bins and updates thresholds; removing the final node does not release bins. Count==0 alone cannot model this distinction.
RemoveAll holds the automatic-rehash lock, so it retains bin count and does not recalculate thresholds while freeing nodes.

Native x86 InitHashTable converts unsigned bin count through x87 into a stored f32, then multiplies in x87 and calls __ftol2 (64-bit return; EAX retained for size_t), high before low. This is NOT the __ftol2_sse signed-i32 helper used for font heights.

Native x86 PickSize converts count to a stored f32, divides by 0.75 in x87, and calls __ftol2 without rounding the division result to f32 first. Rust currently rounds through f32 and uses saturating casts. Large-count reachability and allocation failure must stay qualified.

Cache high/low thresholds; recompute on constructor, logical first allocation and actual rehash only. RemoveAll retains bin count and cached thresholds but requires initialization on reuse. Removing the last node retains initialized bins.
Portable default and scratch Documents do not run host callbacks. Clones retain the static arithmetic service, cached thresholds and logical initialization state.

x86: unsigned count conversion, f32 spill, x87 products/division and __ftol2 retaining EAX. EDI holds the live local threshold scratch array across the exact callee-preserved helper. x64: scalar SSE f32 conversion/product/division and native truncation.
